rule.description: Package-runner identity and runner-specific dispatch must be owned by a single module (the module defining the Runner enum, src/cli/utils.ts); the smell is the same runner knowledge implemented independently in two or more production modules.

checks.description: Detect a raw 'npm'/'yarn' string literal used as an expression and locally re-typed to the Runner type (TSAsExpression/TSTypeAssertion), re-deriving runner identity instead of using the shared Runner enum member.
checks.detected_relation: producer stage -> locally re-derived runner identity
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The stage that is supposed to only report which runner the user selected instead re-implements the identity mapping itself, so a change to runner identity representation must be repeated at every selection site.

matches.evidence: the non-interactive runner selection re-derives the yarn identity as a re-typed literal: ('yarn' as Runner) in the true branch of the --yarn option mapping.
the non-interactive runner selection re-derives the npm identity as a re-typed literal: ('npm' as Runner) in the false branch of the --yarn option mapping.
the runner question's first choice pairs the 'npm' label with a raw inquirer value re-typed as Runner ({ name: 'npm', value: 'npm' as Runner }) instead of a Runner member.
the runner question's second choice pairs the 'yarn' label with a raw inquirer value re-typed as Runner ({ name: 'yarn', value: 'yarn' as Runner }) instead of a Runner member.

checks.description: Detect an object expression serving as a per-module runner dispatch/value table whose raw (non-computed) keys include both runner identities 'npm' and 'yarn'.
checks.detected_relation: consumer stage -> private per-module copy of runner-keyed dispatch or configuration data
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The table encodes runner-to-outcome knowledge locally in whichever module declares it, so extending or renaming the runner set requires editing every module that carries a copy; enum-keyed tables or values obtained from the shared Runner enum do not match.

matches.evidence: module-level table const runnerInstallArguments = { npm: ['install'], yarn: [] } at line 135, consulted by the install factory via runnerInstallArguments[runner] to decide the spawned command's arguments.

module-level table const runnerResetHardScripts = { npm: undefined, yarn: 'git clean -dfx && git reset --hard && yarn' } at line 28, consumed in typescriptStarter to conditionally override the generated project's reset-hard script.
module-level table const runnerIgnoredLockfile = { npm: 'yarn.lock', yarn: 'package-lock.json' } at line 39, consumed in typescriptStarter for the generated .gitignore lockfile entry replacement.

checks.description: Detect a ===/!== comparison (or a case test) that dispatches a runner value against the raw literal 'npm' or 'yarn' string instead of a shared Runner enum member.
checks.detected_relation: consumer stage -> raw runner identity comparison
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Branching on a locally spelled runner identity duplicates the identity knowledge at the branch site, so the same conceptual runner-set change must add or adjust each raw comparison by hand.

matches.evidence: the generated .gitignore lockfile adaptation is guarded by if ((runner as string) === 'yarn') at line 177, comparing a widened runner value against a raw runner literal instead of a Runner enum member.

excluded.reason: The enum member values Npm = 'npm' and Yarn = 'yarn' are the canonical runner identity source other modules should reuse, not duplicates; the rule deliberately does not match enum member initializers.
The meow usage text mentions npm/yarn and the install flag; usage strings never dispatch on runner identity, so raw runner words in help text are not matches.

The string passed as the spawn target ('npm'/'yarn') is a command name selected via a valid runner dispatch (enum member or owner-provided value); it is the usage of the identity, not a re-statement of runner knowledge.
The literal 'git clean -dfx && git reset --hard && yarn' ends in the runner command name as data supplied to the generated project, not a runner-identity decision.
